document.title: Task 2 · Children and advertising
document.text:
Advertising directed at children raises concerns because young audiences may not recognise the commercial purpose of a message. I support strong restrictions on advertising that exploits this vulnerability, especially for harmful products. However, a complete ban on every message about a product for children would be difficult to define and enforce fairly.

Children often have less experience than adults in evaluating persuasive claims. A colourful advert featuring a familiar character may make a product seem desirable without explaining its cost or limitations. This can place pressure on parents and encourage children to connect ownership with social acceptance. The concern is particularly strong when adverts promote foods of poor nutritional value or appear repeatedly within games and videos. In these cases, commercial messages can be closely mixed with entertainment, making their purpose even harder to identify.

For this reason, governments should prohibit manipulative techniques and require clear separation between advertising and other content. Platforms should not be allowed to use detailed behavioural profiles to target young children, and companies should be accountable for misleading claims. Schools and parents can also help children understand how advertising works, although education alone cannot remove the imbalance between a child and a professional marketing organisation. Regulation is therefore necessary even when families take an active role in media use.

A universal ban, on the other hand, could include relatively harmless information about books, educational materials or local activities. The practical challenge is to distinguish useful information from aggressive persuasion without creating rules that are too vague to apply. In conclusion, I agree with banning advertising practices that exploit children, but favour targeted restrictions over an absolute prohibition. Effective protection should focus on the methods used, the products promoted and the age of the audience, supported by consistent enforcement across television and digital media.
document.prompt:
WRITING TASK 2
Allow about 40 minutes.

Advertising aimed at children should be banned. To what extent do you agree or disagree?

Support your answer with reasons and relevant examples. Write at least 250 words.
PPB! original practice material.

annotations.quote: Advertising directed at children raises concerns because young audiences may not recognise the commercial purpose of a message.
annotations.label: Position and scope
annotations.body: Separates a ban on exploitative practices from a ban on all product information. This precise distinction keeps the qualified disagreement consistent.

annotations.quote: Children often have less experience than adults in evaluating persuasive claims.
annotations.label: Developed argument
annotations.body: Explains children’s difficulty recognising commercial intent, then links it to entertainment-based advertising. The paragraph focuses on vulnerability, not an unsupported claim that all adverts are harmful.

annotations.quote: For this reason, governments should prohibit manipulative techniques and require clear separation between advertising and other content.
annotations.label: Counterpoint and response
annotations.body: Proposes enforceable restrictions and explains why education alone is insufficient. This makes the response more developed than a general appeal for parents to supervise children.

annotations.quote: A universal ban, on the other hand, could include relatively harmless information about books, educational materials or local activities.
annotations.label: Synthesis
annotations.body: The books-and-activities counterexample tests the scope of an absolute ban. The conclusion gives three concrete criteria for a targeted policy.
